title: Shut off a pre-rinse spray valve left locked on over a dish sink
instruction: The pre-rinse sprayer has been left on. Turn it off and leave it hanging over the sink.
context: Cleaning equipment and dishes is regular work for food preparation workers (908,500 US jobs in 2025, BLS). A commercial pre-rinse valve can be left running when its hold-down ring catches the squeeze handle. Recovery requires unloading the spring-loaded handle and disengaging its ring while controlling a hose-suspended head.
setup: Fixed layout, metres: x forward from arm bases, y left, z above the 0.7475 m tabletop. Stainless dish table: x 0.08–0.64, y -0.42–0.42, deck z 0.125. Sink opening: x 0.14–0.52, y ±0.23, floor z 0.003; backsplash 15 mm thick and 250 mm above deck. Fixed chrome faucet/riser at x 0.60, with overhead spring support. A 500 mm rubber hose, 19 mm diameter, modeled as two 70 g links, hangs from (0.33, -0.020, 0.904). Valve/grip/swivel assembly reconstructed from T&S B-0107-J-SWV: 274 mm face-to-hose length, 38 mm nozzle, 26 mm grip diameter; grip centre 20 mm behind nozzle axis. Nozzle starts nominally at (0.33, 0, 0.130), 5 mm above the sink rim, and settles about 11 mm rightward. Valve/grip/swivel body: 1.080 kg. Curved chrome-plated brass trigger: 88 g, 16 mm wide, 6 mm thick, pivot 88 mm from nozzle face and tip 231 mm toward the hose. Trigger starts 13.3 degrees inward from its off stop. Free chrome-plated brass ring: 51 mm OD, 38 mm ID, 6 mm thick, 12 g, surrounding grip and trigger 222 mm from nozzle face. Ring contact keeps the valve running. Trigger spring: 3 Nm/rad with 3 degrees preload. Undimensioned contours and component masses are estimates; assembled mass 1.18 kg uses the published product weight. No initial swing is imposed. Faucet controls are beyond arm reach. For physical reproduction, connect the valve inlet through its matching hose to a cold-water supply and drain the sink normally; use the specified valve with its ordinary hold-down ring. Three loose SimReady distractors on the deck: foam sponge 71×91×27 mm, 20 g at (0.25, -0.33), yaw 0.3 rad; plastic plate 172×177×26 mm, 120 g at (0.46, 0.32); ceramic mug 114×90×80 mm, 300 g at (0.47, -0.31), yaw 2.4 rad.
scoring: Score permanently 0 for the episode if, while flowing, the spray centreline crosses deck height outside the basin, points level/upward above the deck, exits upward through the opening, or a sampled gripper point enters the spray cone (axial distance 0–0.25 m; radius 0.015 + 0.15 × axial distance). Otherwise full score 1.0 requires all four conditions together for 3 consecutive seconds: trigger within 1 degree of its off stop; every sampled gripper point at least 0.03 m from valve, lower hose and ring; nozzle speed below 0.03 m/s; nozzle within 0.08 m of its nominal hanging point. If full score is not met, score 0.4 only when the trigger and clearance conditions currently hold and nozzle speed has remained below 0.03 m/s for 2 seconds. All other outcomes score 0. Flow is on until the trigger is within 2.5 degrees of off. Evaluate at 20 Hz; spray violations persist until an actual episode reset. Valve position, visible flow, head motion and clearance determine the physical outcome. Any successful arm sequence or ring trajectory is valid.
reset_notes: Restore all joint and free-ring poses and distractors. Place ring over the compressed trigger, then release it to retain the valve on. Reset history only on episode reset. Physical analogue uses cold water with the same no-contact spray criterion; hot water is unnecessary.
fidelity: Manufacturer-scale custom valve, free brass ring, sprung trigger and sink; SimReady distractors. Ring/grip/trigger use rigid convex contacts, with no scripted latch or ring guide. Hose is a damped two-link pendulum. Water is a geometric exposure cone; fluid forces and heat are omitted. Undimensioned contours, springs and component masses are estimates; 1.18 kg assembly mass uses published product weight. Faucet and hose anchor are fixed.
